title: JavaScript Functions & Execution Scope
description: Master first-class functions in JavaScript: declarations vs expressions, arrow functions, parameters, return statements, and local scope boundaries.

objectives.statement: Declare and invoke named and arrow functions with arguments and return values.
Explain how function execution creates a local variable scope.

content.title: Functions: The Verbs of JavaScript
content.hook: Functions are reusable blocks of logic that turn raw data inputs into meaningful outputs and side-effects.
content.context: In JavaScript, functions are first-class values that can be stored in variables, passed to other functions as callbacks, and returned dynamically.
goals: Write clean function declarations and arrow functions.
Distinguish returning a value from logging to the console.

content.title: Parameters, Return Values, and Scope
content.text: When a function is called, JavaScript allocates a local execution context. Variables declared inside with let or const are inaccessible from outside (block/function scope). To send computation results back to the caller, use the return keyword.

callout.text: Do not confuse console.log(val) with return val. console.log prints to developer tools, while return hands the value back to the caller.

content.keyTakeaway: Functions encapsulate computation and create isolated variable environments.

content.title: Three Syntaxes for Writing Functions
content.description: Notice the subtle differences between function declaration, function expression, and arrow function syntax.

content.prompt: What will be printed to the console when this script runs?
content.explanation: createMultiplier returns an inner arrow function that multiplies its argument by 3. triple(5) calculates 5 * 3 = 15.

feedback.incorrect: Trace the execution: createMultiplier(3) returns (value) => value * 3. Then triple(5) evaluates 5 * 3.

content.title: Write a Temperature Converter
content.prompt: Implement the function celsiusToFahrenheit(celsius) that returns the Fahrenheit equivalent using the formula: (celsius * 9 / 5) + 32.

feedback.correct: Excellent! celsiusToFahrenheit correctly calculates temperature conversions.

content.title: Module Summary
takeaways: Functions can be declared with standard function keywords or concise arrow syntax.
Parameters allow passing dynamic inputs; default parameters prevent undefined errors.
return transmits computed output back to the caller; console.log is for logging only.
